highlights.title: Trump Administration Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Lawsuit
highlights.summary: The US government wrote a letter in support of OpenAI’s argument that training AI on others' intellectual property is fair use.
body: The Trump Administration just took OpenAI’s side in the artificial intelligence company’s legal battle with the New York Times.

The media juggernaut sued OpenAI and Microsoft in 2023, alleging that the companies had violated copyright law by training their AI tools on its articles without permission. Now, the government has stepped in, arguing that OpenAI’s actions were within bounds.

The letter argued that the Times’ definition of fair use is “inconsistent” with current copyright law, and that a win for the paper could have disastrous consequences. “Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility,” lawyers for the government wrote.
While the letter focuses on the New York Times and OpenAI, the government noted that its arguments apply to all of the parties in this case and related cases, including other publishers and authors.
points: The US government wrote a letter in support of OpenAI’s argument that training AI on others' intellectual property is fair use.
The Trump Administration just took OpenAI’s side in the artificial intelligence company’s legal battle with the New York Times.

highlights.title: Brütal Legend Is Still Double Fine's Best Game, Sequel or Not
highlights.summary: Double Fine’s new $400K Kickstarter has a stretch goal that reads like either a dare or a joke, I can’t decide which: Raise $100 million for the studio’s upcoming Amnesia Fortnight game jam, and the studio will make Brütal Legend 2.
body: That’s fabulous, we love to see new games being made, a crowdsourced upwelling of affection for a rad IP will always get me, and I get the dopamine of seeing a progress bar creep to the right, but I think this distracts from the bigger picture: Since the perfect Brütal Legend game already exists, do we need a sequel? Do we really want a sequel? Or is it time to admit that despite any very publicized crowdfunding goals, we’re probably not getting one? Admitting this would free us up to play Double Fine’s best game again, which is the ideal outcome here, because the first and only Brütal Legend was a wild ride.

highlights.title: These Russian Mathematicians Taught AI Models How to Talk to Each Other Without Using Words
highlights.summary: A startup called Mostik has a wild new approach to combining the capabilities of AI models.
body: I recently met with some brilliant Russian mathematicians who showed me a way for artificial intelligence models to communicate via something akin to machine telepathy.

The mathematicians work for a startup called Mostik—the Russian word for bridge. It’s a nod to the group’s approach, which allows different models to interact using the mathematical values found in their weights —the things that determine how a prompt gets turned into an output. In practice, this means the capabilities of a larger model can be fed to a smaller model to ramp up its intelligence much more efficiently.

The startup used the approach to build a model that has rocketed to the top of ARC-AGI 3, a notoriously difficult competition for AI models. (They wouldn’t tell me more because they want to win the contest.) To demonstrate the idea, however, they also created a bridge between two Chinese open-weight models: the largest version of GLM-5.2, which has 753 billion parameters; and a 4-billion-parameter version of Qwen-3.5 that can run on a mobile device. The resulting hybrid system costs one-twentieth of the full GLM model, and its performance is exactly halfway between the two.
points: A startup called Mostik has a wild new approach to combining the capabilities of AI models.

One-Star Raids will feature Pikachu wearing Cap’s hat, and Three-Star Raids will have the event-exclusive Charizard, Meowscarada, Skeledirge, and Quaquaval. The crossover event runs from Sept. 16 at 10 a.m. to Sept. 22 at 8 p.m. local time.

highlights.title: I thought I was too broken for sex. Here’s how I found pleasure again
highlights.summary: I was forced to examine the idea of sexual pleasure after a tumor was removed from my spinal cord. Ten years ago, my right elbow started to hurt. The internet suggested I had tennis elbow, so I stopped playing tennis.
body: For good measure, I consulted an occupational therapist about my nightly bullet-vibrator routine after reading that golfer’s elbow is common among construction workers who operate heavy-duty vibrating machinery. He listened closely and said he’d note VRI on my patient chart. I asked what VRI meant, eager to end my diagnostic journey. “Vibrator-related injury,” he responded. We busted out laughing.

After three years, weak hands and shaky legs had joined the elbow pain. None of the diagnoses I researched or received (a pinched ulnar nerve, tendinitis and thoracic outlet syndrome) fully explained my symptoms. Eventually, an MRI found a tumor growing inside my spinal cord. One surgeon estimated that without treatment, my body would undergo complete, permanent paralysis from the neck down within a year.

highlights.title: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
highlights.summary: Amazon is trying to combat impersonation scams with a new feature that allows you to use its AI assistant to determine whether an email, text message, or phone call actually came from the company.
body: Alexa for Shopping can compare the message you received ‘against a record of every message Amazon has sent.’

As noted by Amazon, the assistant will only confirm that a message is real if it’s “completely certain.” An example shared by Amazon shows a customer asking, “Did Amazon just text me an OTP from 98626? Message came around 4:50pm.” Alexa for Shopping responds by confirming that Amazon actually did send the message, saying, “This was a genuine One Time Password from Amazon.”

If Alexa for Shopping determines a message isn’t from Amazon, it will instruct customers to check their orders in the app and contact Amazon’s support team directly. The company launched a similar feature earlier this year that lets you forward suspicious messages to “verify@amazon.com” to check if they’re real.
This isn’t the only recent update Amazon has launched for Alexa for Shopping, as it added an “Update Me When” feature that can now help you track new product releases as well.

highlights.title: Iconic Banjo-Kazooie composer is more hopeful about a sequel these days, but knows "like three companies" have already been turned down
highlights.summary: Grant Kirkhope - the iconic video game composer behind the Donkey Kong Rap and the Banjo-Kazooie games - thinks a potential Banjo-Threeie is slightly more likely now.
body: Almost three decades have passed since Banjo-Kazooie's last mainline platformer flapped onto the N64 and it's been almost 20 years since Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts flopped onto the Xbox 360, but it's never too late for another adventure with the bird and bear.

Speaking to FRVR, Kirkhope explained that he used to feel there was "zero chance of another Banjo-Kazooie game." Nowadays, that sentiment's been upgraded to a "slight chance" because he thinks Rare's updated leadership could be more receptive to an outside developer spearheading a threequel.

"Rare just typically say no to everything," the composer explained. "I've known people present cartoons to them, all sorts of ideas, and they just say no to everything." But since former studio head Craig Duncan stepped down from his role at Xbox Game Studios, Kirkhope reckons Rare might be "a little bit different right now" and "a bit more open to discussion."

highlights.title: King hails 'unprecedented' Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London
highlights.summary: British and French leaders will be at the British Museum to see the exhibition of the historic Bayeux Tapestry.
body: King Charles has hailed the "unprecedented loan" of the Bayeux Tapestry to the British Museum, calling it the "best possible symbol" of the closeness between the UK and France.

After viewing the medieval tapestry in London on Wednesday a week before it goes on public display, he spoke in French and English to guests including President Emmanuel Macron of France and Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
The King said he was the direct descendant of one of the key figures in the tapestry, William, Duke of Normandy, whose army invaded and defeated King Harold at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
The tapestry "tells the story of the beginning of what I like to think of as the French side of my family's history in these islands", he added.

highlights.title: ICE Plans to Pay $5 Million to Create National Voting Database
highlights.summary: As part of a broader DHS surge to investigate alleged voter fraud, ICE has announced it plans to pay up to $5 million to create what amounts to a federal voter database.
body: In a bid to tackle alleged voter fraud, Immigration and Customs Enforcement is preparing to award a contract worth up to $5 million to a company that will create a massive national database of voters.

ICE first detailed what the contract would entail in a document published last week. “The purpose of this acquisition is for the handling and secure delivery of publicly available voter registration files and voter history files to support Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) fraud detection and data segmentation activities,” the document reads.

The document states that the successful contractor won’t be asked to collect and share party affiliation data fields for voters but that could change if “explicitly directed in writing by the contracting officer.” That contracting officer is listed as Michael Royer, section chief at Homeland Security Investigations, the investigative unit within ICE. ICE, DHS, and Royer did not respond to a request for comment.

It’s one of the first-round matches that didn’t get on yesterday.

The match point is, at least, on Choinski’s serve, but the Brit bashes a forehand long and this rain-delayed opening-round match is over. highlights.title: 1001: Threads of Mizan Was One of Gamescom 2026’s Best Action Games
highlights.summary: 1001: Threads of Mizan was, as game director Scott Lussier said to me in an interview at Gamescom 2026, the "greatest secret ever kept." The gaming industry has a habit of leaking news about upcoming games and therefore spoiling the surprise, so when the trailer for Mizan was shown during Opening…
body: The only problem with the reveal trailer was that while it wears its Arabian Nights inspiration on its sleeve, it gave no indication as to its genre, mission structure, story, and so on. I've played the game now, in a 15-minute session behind closed doors. While I only got to experience a brief section of one level, Lussier also explained how the rest of the game will work.

"What we're building here is a single-player action adventure game that gets better with your friends," he told me. "We have created our own world that is inspired largely by the tales of Arabian folklore, and we're weaving the world of Arabian Nights inside there. It's about flying on carpets, fighting colossal enemies, and doing it with your friends while also experiencing stories inside of stories."

…but it does have another dynamic in play: flight combat. After we took down the Sand Knight, a mini-boss that required plenty of synergy between our trio to dodge his attacks and pummel him together when he was staggered, the demo flung us directly into the headline act, a boss fight against a jinn named Nazjush.

highlights.title: What did I learn in the kitchen this week? The longer it takes to cook, the less you want to eat it | Adrian Chiles
highlights.summary: After grilling, skinning, chopping and stirring, stirring, stirring, my feelings towards my favourite Balkan relish, ajvar, changed. Those Macedonian nans must be made of girders.
body: I f you ever meet someone from North Macedonia and find yourself short of conversation, then one word will get things going nicely. That word is ajvar. Pronounce it “Ivor”, as in The Engine – not quite right but it’ll do. Depending on who you ask, ajvar is a condiment, spread, sauce or relish. It’s made – also depending on who you ask – with red peppers and aubergine. You can eat it with meat, cheese, fish, vegetables, on toast or, using a large spoon, straight from the jar.

I was accompanying a 13-year-old called Ilijana as she played the British chess grandmaster Nigel Short. This was on the waterfront in Split, Croatia. Long story. All you need to know is that my contribution to the contest was zero. All I could do was try to bond with her somehow, by finding some area of common ground. So I said the magic word: ajvar! This was the conversational equivalent of a chess move – something with a knight perhaps? – which she didn’t see coming. It worked a treat. Suddenly she was all smiles, telling me how her grandma’s ajvar was the best in the world.

Those Macedonian nans must be made of girders.

highlights.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks
highlights.summary: Google hasn't released a frontier-level Gemini Pro AI model since early 2026, but it sure loves rolling out new Gemini Flash variants. Today, Google is announcing its third Flash model release in just six weeks, making it more likely that we'll never see the promised Gemini 3.5 Pro.
body: Gemini 3.8 Flash comes in two variations. There’s the standard Flash, which Google describes as a “workhorse” model that’s good for anything from agentic tasks to software development. Then we have Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, which runs on the same foundations but has been tuned for vulnerability detection and mitigation.

For developers, Google has the same pitch as it did for the 3.7 Flash release just a couple of weeks ago. API access to the model is available at an “introductory rate” through the end of the year: $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens. The regular price will be $1.50 / $7.50, but it’s likely there will be new models available long before the price changes. Google probably sees the lower prices as a necessity given that other AI labs have recently dropped token pricing to keep increasingly wary businesses engaged with AI tools.

Google has offered its usual raft of benchmark numbers, which appear to show Gemini 3.8 Flash competing with (or even beating) larger and more expensive models. The numbers show a marginal improvement over Gemini 3.7 Flash in most tests, but the gains are larger in coding evaluations.
points: Google hasn't released a frontier-level Gemini Pro AI model since early 2026, but it sure loves rolling out new Gemini Flash variants.

highlights.title: The Logical End Point of AI Job Interviews Is Two Bots Talking to Each Other
highlights.summary: Christopher was sick of being ghosted by AI recruiters. So he unleashed ChatGPT on his robot interviewer.
body: Christopher has become accustomed to jumping through the endless hoops of the modern job hunt. Like many government contractors, his work has dried up in the DOGE era. Over the past six months, he has applied to roughly 700 jobs; in the vast majority of cases, he’s heard nothing back.

Five of these applications have gone through “Riley,” an AI recruiter for the IT firm Everforth Apex Systems. The first time Riley reached out, Christopher was excited. It was June, and he had by then realized how difficult the job market was. (Christopher asked that WIRED use only his first name as his job hunt continues.) A text from Riley felt like a rare opportunity to pitch himself, even if his interlocutor was virtual.

During his first call with Riley, Christopher answered questions about his work authorization and his professional background. Riley promised that, if Christopher met the qualifications, someone would be in touch. But a human recruiter never reached out. Nor did the AI agent—until a little over a week later, when Riley texted Christopher about “another opportunity.”

highlights.title: Legion of Super-Heroes #1 Review: Can DC Revitalize Its Most Notoriously Convoluted Franchise?
highlights.summary: Legion of Super-Heroes #1 successfully reboots a storied DC franchise, especially on the strength of its gorgeous visual storytelling. Read our full review.
body: In DC's vast catalog of superhero franchises, The Legion of Super-Heroes has always been arguably the toughest sell for casual readers. Part of that is the dorky Silver Age trappings that have persisted across the decades, but it's mostly down to the sheer size of the massive ensemble cast and the fact that the series is constantly being retooled and rebooted every few years. The very nature of DC's sliding time scale means the future is always in flux, and so we're constantly treated to a different take on this team of idealistic teen heroes.

That all being said, DC has been finding great success in revamping old properties with the DC All In/Next Level initiative, so it only makes sense that the Legion be given the same treatment. And while the prospect of rebooting this convoluted franchise yet again is a little tiresome, the results speak for themselves. This is an engaging and gorgeously rendered entry point into The Legion of Super-Heroes.
points: Legion of Super-Heroes #1 successfully reboots a storied DC franchise, especially on the strength of its gorgeous visual storytelling.

body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

highlights.title: Trump may be forced to reveal secret rules feds use for AI safety testing
highlights.summary: Four federal agencies have been sued amid calls to release information about the secret framework that the Trump administration uses to conduct safety reviews of frontier AI models prior to release.
body: In a Wednesday press release announcing the lawsuit, a nonpartisan nonprofit called Protect Democracy alleged that “almost no details” have been released to the public or Congress. To everyone except a few vague “trusted partners,” it remains unclear what the government’s review process looks like, which companies are involved in constructing the framework, or what legal authority Trump officials have to conduct the reviews.
“Neither the identities of those entities nor the criteria by which they were selected have been made public,” Protect Democracy said.

That’s a problem, Protect Democracy alleged in a statement to Ars, since decisions about “which AI models are approved and released may be the most important policy question of this White House.” And it appears that at least one AI firm, OpenAI, has “negotiated a private agreement with the Federal Government to limit distribution of its cutting-edge AI models to government-vetted partners.”

highlights.title: Disney Was Working on Its Own Smash Bros.-Like Fighting Game, Confirms Ex-Concept Artist
highlights.summary: Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.
body: In 2013, Christiansen posted a slew of artworks to his online portfolio, some of which showed rough sketches of various Disney characters facing off in battle. It sparked the idea that Disney had possibly toyed with a crossover fighting game — something that Christiansen has now confirmed.

Speaking with Time Extension in a September 1 interview, Christiansen opened up about the surprising way Kingdom Hearts helped bring the idea to life, though it ultimately never came to fruition. In fact, it was difficult for Kingdom Hearts to get approved in the first place, as Disney execs were hesitant to combine some of the brand’s most iconic properties.

"Since Kingdom Hearts already kind of broke that mold, producers would say, 'Hey, what if we say they're action figures, and we kind of take the same conceit as Toy Story, but have them fight each other instead?' Then, we can have all these action figures of Disney characters from Tarzan, The Lion King, and Treasure Planet, and it can be this Smash Brothers kind of thing. The title of that concept was 'Disney's Action Figure Face Off."
points: Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.

highlights.title: Samsung's Frame Pro isn't just a gorgeous TV, it opened my eyes to art
highlights.summary: The design-forward TV delivers a performance that few in the category can – while attracting compliments as wall decor. Can’t hear what’s playing on TV? It’s not your ears, it’s the flat screen. These affordable soundbars can help.
body: When they are screening blockbusters, huge TVs are cinematic portals to another world. When they’re off, huge TVs are hideous black mirrors. Samsung has always understood this home decor landmine and aimed to defuse it in 2017 with The Frame, the first-ever “art TV”: a television disguised as a framed painting.

As a female tech editor who spent years appraising the banal designs of 1990s tech, I can palpably remember how thrilled I was to see this innovative melding of form and function, which seemed like a novel luxury at the time. Fast-forward nearly a decade, and Samsung’s pricey niche concept has gone decisively mainstream, with competition from LG, Hisense, TCL and even Amazon.
But Samsung hasn’t been sitting still: The Frame Pro boasts cordless architecture, a matte screen and customizable magnetic bezels.
